headline: Indian shares post longest weekly losing streak as global rate worries weigh
why: Higher US Treasury yields and Fed rate hike fears dent global investor sentiment.
Rising crude oil prices exacerbate inflation concerns for net-importer India.
Weakness in IT majors and Tata group stocks drags down benchmark indices.
Global investor sentiment plunges to a 16-month low according to AAII survey.
whatHappening: Indian equity markets post their longest weekly losing streak in six years.
Sensex and Nifty trade mixed amid sharp sectoral divergence in IT and Banking.
State Bank of India estimates ₹5 trillion potential notional profit from FCNR(B) for banks over 5 years.
Paytm remains in market focus amid broader stock volatility and opening updates.

summary:
Indian benchmark indices faced their longest weekly losing streak in six years amid rising US Treasury yields and elevated crude oil prices.
Weakness in IT and Tata group stocks pulled down the Sensex, while Paytm and SBI remained in focus due to stock-specific triggers.
Global headwinds and rate hike fears continue to depress investor sentiment to multi-month lows.
